title: Open Road (Placeholder Mirror Example)
description: An original example of the placeholder-mirror pattern: the opening prompt asks the player a chain of ${questions}, and the same text is duplicated into Plot Essentials so the player's answers stay in always-on context after the prompt scrolls out of history. Zero story cards.
prompt: You and two companions are halfway through a road trip with no destination. Your name is ${What is your character's name?}. You are a ${How old is your character, and what are they like? Example: 24, restless and broke.}. Riding with you is ${Who is the first companion, and how do you know them?}, and ${Who is the second companion, and how do you know them?}. You are travelling in a ${What are you travelling in? Example: a rusted orange van named Clementine.}, and right now you are ${Where are you right now, and what just happened? Example: pulled over at a desert gas station at 2am because the engine started smoking.}.
plotEssentials: /remember Your name is ${What is your character's name?}. You are a ${How old is your character, and what are they like? Example: 24, restless and broke.}. Riding with you is ${Who is the first companion, and how do you know them?}, and ${Who is the second companion, and how do you know them?}. You are travelling in a ${What are you travelling in? Example: a rusted orange van named Clementine.}.
authorsNote:
Perspective: second person, present tense.
Warm and character-driven; let the companions have their own opinions.
